name: RDSI-The-Hidden-Mathematics-Behind-the-Clock
description: Shifting from 0-based to 1-based indexing eliminates complex software workarounds. Pure algebra replaces bitwise hacks and costly conditional branches with direct arithmetic. No logical jumps. No off-by-one errors. Just a clean, deterministic execution path built into the formula itself.

paragraphs: How a huge number becomes something you can read, and why one small choice, counting from 1 instead of 0, removes a whole family of bugs.
📘 Main paper · 📄 Clock paper · 🔗 Interactive demo · 📋 How to cite

Most software counts positions from 0: for a 12-hour dial, positions 0 to 11. That looks harmless, but the end of one cycle and the start of the next get the same number. Midnight is both the end of one day and the start of the next. Programmers know the result as the "off-by-one error".
features: Dates and times. Whenever a large number becomes something readable, the same layered structure is at work: 45,296,789 ms → 12:34:56.789, 1,234,567 bytes → 1.23 MB, 20260917 → 17 September 2026. Many timestamp bugs come…
Teaching. Everyone understands that 3 hours after 11 o'clock is 2 o'clock. That is the remainder rule (14 mod 12 = 2), and the clock makes it obvious.
A general lesson. A layered system can be built to explore all combinations or to leave no room for doubt. It cannot do both at once.
